summary: The month's one real reversal is in glycan control. categories.name: PAT & Spectroscopic Process Control
categories.synthesis: The month's substance is in getting a spectral model to survive contact with more than one process. BioOps supplies what this category has been missing for two months, an implemented rather than argued closed loop: version-controlled model registries, containerized deployment and CI/CD sitting behind PAT-driven feedback control, hybrid model-based glucose feeding and adaptive phase transitions across geographically distributed bioreactors, albeit with no control performance quantified. Cutting against both, the industrial fed-batch benchmarking study found that the tightly controlled variables, glucose and pH, contributed almost nothing to titer prediction within the operating range while elapsed culture time, total cell density, culture volume and the glutamine/glutamate pair carried it, which is an argument for not spending spectral capacity on loops you already hold at setpoint. The Raman-NIR cross-attention model posts the month's best numbers, R2 = 0.991 and RMSE 1.09 g/L for glucose, on 142 records of microbial broth, so it is an architecture to watch rather than a result. items.title: Cross-attention fusion of Raman and NIR spectra for glucose soft sensing in fed-batch fermentation.
items.summary: A dual-stream cross-attention Transformer (DS-CAT) fused Raman and NIR spectra from 142 synchronized records of fermentation broth, after Savitzky-Golay first-derivative and SNV preprocessing, to predict glucose. On the test set it reached R2 = 0.991, RMSE 1.09 g/L and MAE 0.89 g/L, beating PLSR, GBRT, CNN and TCN under the same protocol, with five-fold validation at R2 = 0.988 +/- 0.009. Perturbation analysis showed the prediction leaned on the Raman stream, with 1122-1335 cm-1 the most sensitive interval.
items.why_it_matters: The fusion architecture is worth watching but 142 records of microbial broth is nothing like a CHO calibration set, so the transferable content is the Raman band sensitivity finding rather than the accuracy claim.

items.title: Data-Driven Approach for Bioreactor Monitoring and Prediction in Monoclonal Antibody Production.
items.summary: A previously published industrial fed-batch mAb dataset was rebuilt end to end: eight supervised regressors were compared for imputation, with LightGBM selected because it preserved all observed measurements exactly and reproduced both marginal distributions and multivariate geometry better than a published dual-hybrid method. Thirty-four single and stacked models were then benchmarked for pointwise titer soft sensing (test R2 up to 0.98) and early prediction of final titer from days 1-7 (0.93), with nonlinear tree ensembles beating linear and kernel models and stacking adding modest consistent gains. items.why_it_matters: The variable importance result is the usable part: the loops you hold tightly at setpoint carry almost no predictive information, so feed a titer soft sensor culture age, cell mass, volume and the glutamine/glutamate pair instead.

items.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Generic Raman Model for Commercial-Scale Cell Culture Process Monitoring.
items.summary: In-line Raman spectra from four distinct 1500-L commercial CHO fed-batch processes were aggregated into one generic model; 15 combinations of regression algorithm and feature selection were screened, then representative pipelines were tested under repeated batch-level validation splits. items.why_it_matters: First commercial-scale evidence that one Raman calibration can span multiple products, with the honest limit attached - budget a small labeled set per new process rather than assuming a global model removes recalibration.

items.title: BioOps: Enabling MLOps for scalable and flexible model-centric process control in biopharmaceutical development.
items.summary: BioOps is a modular automation framework for advanced process control that imports MLOps practice into the control stack: version-controlled model registries, containerized deployment and CI/CD pipelines, with model development explicitly decoupled from model execution so models and control strategies can be deployed and refined without vendor-specific integration. Case studies across a geographically distributed set of bioreactors cover PAT-driven feedback control, hybrid model-based nutrient and glucose feeding, adaptive phase transitions and cross-scale deployment, with traceability and model lifecycle management embedded.

items.title: Sensitive and derivatization-free amino acid analysis using liquid chromatography-Raman spectroscopy.
items.summary: Liquid chromatography coupled to Raman detection via post-column spotting and solvent evaporation detected all 20 amino acids at nanogram level without derivatization, with MCR-ALS deconvolution resolving co-eluting compounds and distinct vibrational fingerprints discriminating lysine modifications. items.why_it_matters: An offline amino acid method that adds structural specificity without a derivatization step, relevant if you are chasing a specific feed component or a lysine modification rather than running a full panel.

items.title: [Machine learning-based optimization strategies for fermentation processes].
items.venue: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
items.summary: A review of machine learning in microbial fermentation control, tracing a closed loop from data perception through to decision-making: modeling workflows built to counter the black-box and data-lag limits of purely data-driven models, a comparison of process analytical technologies that places Raman at the center of real-time monitoring, and semi-supervised learning plus data augmentation as responses to scarce labeled samples. items.why_it_matters: Nothing to act on - a microbial fermentation review whose only transferable content is the semi-supervised and data-augmentation framing for Raman label scarcity.

items.title: A Review on Applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Monoclonal Antibody (mAb) Manufacturing.
items.summary: A review surveying artificial intelligence applications across mAb manufacturing - upstream and downstream processing, process control, optimization, product property monitoring and regulatory compliance - with case studies on predictive modeling for cell culture optimization, media formulation and bioreactor control, plus process monitoring, fault detection and real-time decision-making.
items.why_it_matters: A broad survey with no new data; useful only as a citation for an internal AI strategy document.

items.title: Electrical Signatures of Life: A Review of Cell Electrophysiology and Dielectric Analysis (2015-2026).
items.summary: A review of cell electrophysiology and dielectric analysis covering 2015-2026, organized around permittivity, conductivity, membrane capacitance, polarizability and surface charge as the properties that set how cells respond to applied electric fields, and surveying electrokinetic platforms for rapid label-free cellular assessment across clinical, environmental and industrial bioprocessing contexts.

items.title: Sensing the future of cell therapy manufacturing.

categories.name: Upstream Process Development
categories.synthesis: Upstream this month is about moving a process between scales and modes rather than finding a new lever, and the two most useful results are each half negative. items.title: A Benchmark Fed-Batch Bioprocess for Production of cNISTmAb using NISTCHO.

items.title: Next-gen glycoengineering: combining cellular and metabolic engineering to fine-tune mAb β1,4-galactosylation

items.why_it_matters: Galactosylation becomes a dialable parameter rather than a drifting attribute, but the dose transfers neither between hosts nor between flasks and a fed-batch bioreactor - normalize to cells and to post-feed secretion or you will mis-dose by an order of magnitude.

items.title: Implementing an Intensified Dynamic Perfusion Process for Biologics Manufacturing at Scale and Continued Development.
items.summary: The high-intensity, low-volume perfusion (HILVOP) process was implemented at 100 L pilot and 500 L manufacturing scale for early clinical supply, using a dynamic two-stage strategy of cell-controlled perfusion during growth followed by product removal by tangential flow filtration during an intensified production phase, across multiple CHO cell lines. items.why_it_matters: The specific fixes that beat fouling at 500 L are directly actionable, and the framing matters as much: at manufacturing scale the limiting variable was the retention device, not the cell line or the feed.

items.title: A kinetically constrained dynamic flux balance analysis model predicts diverse CHO-cell culture process modes and conditions.

items.title: Mechanistic Digital Model for Real-Time Monitoring and Optimization of Adenovirus Production.
items.summary: Working on adenovirus production, the authors screened indicators of the cell density effect and identified glucose availability per cell at time of infection as the most effective proxy, then built an age-structured mechanistic model linking glucose and viable cell density to viral production while reproducing the density/productivity trade-off. The model predicted viral particle titers in batch and fed-batch at RMSE 0.39 log10 IVP/mL for infectious particles and 0.20 log10 VP/mL for total particles, about 2.6 and 2.0 times the respective assay standard deviations.

items.title: [Data-mechanism integrated optimization and preliminary scale-up study of feeding process in penicillin fermentation].
items.venue: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
items.summary: Historical data from 325 penicillin batches in a 156 m3 industrial fermenter were screened by curve similarity and correlation analysis against harvest titer, maximum specific production rate and the onset of secondary metabolism, identifying cumulative glucose feeding amount and dilution rate as the key drivers of performance. A high late-stage dilution rate sustained high specific growth rate and suppressed penicillin accumulation, while lower glucose feeding and reduced dilution let growth rate fall and raised production capacity. A viable cell electrode was then used for online biomass monitoring in a 50 L system, and dynamic growth-rate regulation through higher feed glucose concentration and an optimized feed rate raised glucose conversion efficiency 22.06 percent, titer 16.10 percent and fermentation index 16.42 percent.
items.why_it_matters: A clean industrial demonstration that feed volume, not only feed composition, sets specific growth rate and therefore the growth-versus-production split - and a reminder that cumulative feed volume is a controlled variable many groups do not track as one.

items.title: Enabling Bioprocess Upscaling Prediction Through Hybrid Modelling and Transfer Learning Under Small-Data Scenarios.
items.summary: Hybrid modeling was combined with transfer learning to predict industrial-scale dynamics from a high-fidelity model built on limited lab-scale data and adapted using pilot-scale information only. On a real yeast fermentation case the framework reached 23.2 percent mean absolute percentage error at industrial scale. The study also found that the greyness of the hybrid model - how much mechanism versus how much learned function - decisively governs both predictive accuracy and whether transfer learning is feasible at all, and that the optimal level under data scarcity differs from the data-rich case.
items.why_it_matters: The greyness finding is the usable one: do not port a hybrid structure validated on a data-rich process into a thin one, because the right mechanistic/empirical balance changes with how much data you have.

items.title: Developing affordable monoclonal antibodies for LMICs through high performance manufacturing processes and LMIC based commercial manufacturing.
items.summary: High-productivity, high-yield fed-batch production was demonstrated with clonal variants of ZAC-3, a mAb against the conserved core and lipid A region of Vibrio cholerae lipopolysaccharide, and those run data were then extrapolated to a continuous manufacturing approach to argue a viable path to low-cost commercial supply, further reduced by manufacturing in an LMIC-based GMP facility.
items.why_it_matters: The continuous manufacturing economics are extrapolated from fed-batch data rather than demonstrated, so read this as a COGS argument for low-dose infectious-disease mAbs rather than as process evidence.

items.title: Evaluation of media intensification strategies in perfusion.
items.summary: Two media intensification strategies aimed at cutting perfusion rate by up to 30 percent were compared: a concentrated basal formulation and a commercial perfusion-rate-reducing supplement. Direct concentration stalled cell growth by raising osmolality and ultimately lowered viability, while the supplement maintained viability and productivity with no significant product quality impact, and the result generalized to a different medium and clone. Cell cycle analysis showed both strategies arrest cells in G0/G1, but the supplement arrested proliferation more effectively, suggesting a larger shift from growth-driven glycolytic cells to production-driven oxidative metabolism.
items.why_it_matters: Concentrating the perfusion medium is the obvious way to cut volumetric media spend and this says it fails on osmolality; the G0/G1 and oxidative-shift reading also tells you to measure cell cycle distribution, not just VCD and titer, when evaluating any perfusion rate reduction.

items.title: Upstream process optimization and its critical role in chimpanzee adenoviral vector clinical drug development: lessons learned from VRON-0200 manufacturing.
items.summary: During development of VRON-0200, a chimpanzee adenoviral (AdC) vector immunotherapy for chronic hepatitis B, the authors found that upstream process optimization rather than downstream purification drove crude harvest quality and final drug product attributes. Iterative refinement of permissive cell growth cycles, time of harvest and multiplicity of infection, guided by a tiered analytical strategy, delivered high-purity harvests with better infectivity ratios, lower host cell residuals and fewer product-related impurities, reducing downstream processing demand; the resulting process supported GMP production and a Phase 1b readout showing safety, tolerability and significant anti-HBV activity.
items.why_it_matters: An explicit upstream-first argument against polishing your way out of a dirty harvest, with the levers named (growth cycles, harvest timing, MOI) and a clinical-stage case attached - exactly the argument DSP counterparts tend to resist.

items.title: DNA concentration in harvest affects retrovirus clearance capabilities of protein A chromatography.
items.summary: A dataset of virus spiking studies suggested a correlation between DNA content in harvest cell culture fluid and the log reduction value of Protein A chromatography, which was then tested directly with murine leukemia virus and retrovirus-like particles spiked into starting material from three different mAbs. Higher HCCF DNA levels enhanced LRV for both particle types, a trend confirmed with RVLP spiked into pure mAb, and Protein A wash buffers containing a detergent or a reducing agent further improved LRV.
items.why_it_matters: If you remove DNA early with functionalized depth filters or precipitation you may be reducing the retrovirus clearance you claim for Protein A, so the harvest DNA level in your spiking studies has to match what your process actually delivers.

items.title: Going with the flow: peptide affinity membranes for high-throughput, high-yield purification of adenovirus and lentiviral vectors.
items.summary: Cellulose membranes were grafted with hyperbranched polyethyleneimine to amplify reactive group density and then functionalized with peptide affinity ligands for viral vector capture. For adenovirus 5 the AEFFIWNAC membrane gave a 10 percent dynamic binding capacity of 1.6 x 10^11 vg/mL at a 20 second residence time, 89 percent genome recovery and host cell protein LRV 2.21, exceeding the cognate peptide resin in both capacity and productivity; a VSV-G pseudotyped lentiviral vector reached 1.5 x 10^11 vp/mL, 87 percent total and 45 percent transducing particle recovery and LRV 2.18 in about 30 minutes against roughly 2 hours on resin, and Cocal pseudotype gave 91 percent particle and 67 percent functional recovery. Extension to AAV9 showed feasible immobilization and measurable binding but lower capacity than the corresponding resin.
items.why_it_matters: For large viral vectors a membrane now beats the equivalent resin on capacity as well as speed, which removes the usual capacity objection - note the AAV9 exception and the gap between total and transducing particle recovery.

items.title: Integrated Continuous Biomanufacturing of Recombinant Adeno-Associated Virus.

Against conventional batch processing, perfusion improved capsid or vector genome yield depending on the production process, and affinity capture alone brought total DNA down to batch-comparable levels with no measurable loss of impurity clearance or potency.
items.why_it_matters: The notable claim is the unit operations deleted rather than the yield - this is the architecture to borrow when costing a continuous vector process, bearing in mind it is a preprint and the yield benefit was process-dependent.

items.title: Development and Validation of an Antigen-Capture ELISA for Quantitative Detection of Donkey-Origin Rotavirus: Application in Vaccine Manufacturing Process Monitoring.
items.summary: A VP6-based antigen-capture ELISA for donkey-origin rotavirus A was built with rabbit anti-RVA polyclonal IgG for capture and an HRP-conjugated anti-VP6 monoclonal for detection, reaching a 1 ng/mL detection limit with a 1-25 ng/mL linear range, no cross-reactivity against eight common equine pathogens and intra- and inter-assay CVs below 10 percent, with estimates consistent with Western blot densitometry. In process use it supported selection of a 100 kDa ultrafiltration membrane and monitored pilot-scale tangential flow filtration, giving 75.69 percent VP6 recovery and an 18-fold increase in antigen purity.
items.why_it_matters: An in-process antigen assay actually used to choose a TFF membrane and track recovery - the method pattern transfers even though the molecule does not.

items.title: Production of Lentiviral Vectors Encoding the CRISPR-Cas13d System for RNA Targeting.
items.summary: A protocol chapter for producing high-titer third-generation lentiviral vectors carrying a dual-expression cassette for CRISPR-Cas13d and a customizable guide RNA, covering guide cloning, transfection of HEK293T cells with packaging and transfer plasmids, harvest and concentration of viral supernatants, and titer determination.
items.why_it_matters: A bench protocol with no process or scale content; nothing here for a production platform.

items.title: Simulation-Aided Development of Multicolumn Chromatography Processes for Protein-Based Vaccine Production
authors: Alan Deduyer, Eric Forma, Estelle Guiot, Lucrèce Nicoud, David Pfister
items.summary: A trade article arguing that mechanistic modeling supports the design of robust, efficient and scalable multicolumn chromatography for protein-based vaccine production, on the grounds that multicolumn operation improves affinity resin utilization and downstream productivity while reducing facility footprint and buffer consumption. No data, conditions or case results are given in what was published.
items.why_it_matters: Nothing to act on from the summary alone; worth opening only if you are assembling the internal capex case for multicolumn capture on resin cost grounds.

categories.name: Media & Feed Development
categories.synthesis: Two items, neither about a CHO production medium, and that absence is the finding. The RSV G study is worth reading for its mechanism rather than its subject: producing the same glycoprotein in three different media gave marked apparent molecular weight differences that vanished in glycosylation-deficient cells, and higher apparent glycosylation tracked with weaker binding of human F-specific monoclonal antibodies to infected cells - medium choice alone moving a glycan-dependent binding readout, demonstrated in HEK293T and A549. The agricultural by-product review is a cultured-meat and cost-reduction survey whose own listed obstacles, compositional variability and missing scale-up validation, are exactly why none of it is adoptable in a chemically defined platform. Against September's thiazolidine cysteine result this is a step backwards, and nothing has appeared on raw material lot-to-lot variability, trace metals or media stability for three months running - that gap, rather than these two papers, is what characterizes the category right now.

items.title: Cell culture medium influences RSV G protein glycosylation and recognition by monoclonal antibodies.
items.summary: The RSV G ectodomain was produced in HEK293T cells in three different culture media and showed marked differences in apparent molecular weight that disappeared in glycosylation-deficient knockout cells. RSV grown in A549 cells in the same media differed in relative G protein signal in the virus stocks and in virus spread, and higher apparent G glycosylation was associated with lower binding of human F protein-specific monoclonal antibodies to infected cells.
items.why_it_matters: A reminder that medium choice on its own can move glycosylation enough to change antibody recognition - shown on a viral glycoprotein in HEK293T and A549, so treat it as a prompt to look at your own medium-driven glycan variability rather than as CHO evidence.

items.title: Recycling of bioresource by-products for the production of cell culture media: research trends and prospects.
items.venue: Critical reviews in food science and nutrition
items.summary: A review categorizing agricultural by-products into livestock, seafood, plant and secondary-processing groups and mapping them onto basal media, serum substitutes, growth factors, antibiotic alternatives, scaffolds and functional additives via a cross-functional applicability matrix. Livestock-derived sera and plasma proteins supported proliferation comparable to FBS, fish collagen peptides and microalgal extracts showed growth-factor-like activity, plant protein hydrolysates are already used at large scale, and yeast and whey hydrolysates can support serum replacement and media recycling - with compositional variability, long-term safety, scale-up validation and regulatory standardization named as the open problems.
items.why_it_matters: Aimed at cultured meat and cost-driven applications; for a chemically defined CHO platform the compositional variability the review itself flags is precisely why none of it is adoptable.

categories.name: Process Intensification & Continuous Manufacturing
categories.synthesis: Intensification stopped being argued and started being installed, and the constraint sits where August put it, in the hardware around the reactor rather than in the cell. HILVOP ran at 500 L for clinical supply with TFF membrane fouling as the named risk and a specific set of fixes - lower membrane wall shear rate, larger pore size, alternative membrane, reshaped perfusion rate profiles - that delayed transmembrane pressure rise and raised cumulative recovery, while the continuous rAAV preprint sustained five days of perfusion coupled to twin-column affinity capture and dropped lysis, depth filtration and endonuclease treatment from the train. Two results change what intensification has to buy: the dFBA model showed experimentally validated intensified fed-batch reaching fed-batch-equivalent titer in shorter duration, which is space-time yield without extra cell mass and therefore without the precursor tax August's glycan work described, while the perfusion media study found the direct route to lower volumetric media use fails, since concentrating the formulation raises osmolality and stalls growth and only the perfusion-rate-reducing supplement held performance. September's observation that the gap between what this category publishes and what is installed had not closed is partly answered this month - a 500 L perfusion process supplying clinic, and in the trade press a large sponsor calling integrated continuous purification a platform decision for 2027, are installation rather than argument. The remaining items are adjacent: the LMIC mAb paper extrapolates continuous economics from fed-batch run data rather than demonstrating them, and the aqueous two-phase extractive fermentation work is an integration idea with no route into a mAb train.

items.title: Implementing an Intensified Dynamic Perfusion Process for Biologics Manufacturing at Scale and Continued Development.
items.summary: The high-intensity, low-volume perfusion (HILVOP) process was implemented at 100 L pilot and 500 L manufacturing scale for early clinical supply, using a dynamic two-stage strategy of cell-controlled perfusion during growth followed by product removal by tangential flow filtration during an intensified production phase, across multiple CHO cell lines. Early manufacturing runs identified membrane fouling as the key risk, particularly with challenging cell lines; reducing membrane wall shear rate, moving to a larger pore size and an alternative membrane, and refining the perfusion rate profile delayed transmembrane pressure rise, raised cumulative product recovery and cut media consumption. High-density seeding and extension of the productive perfusion phase then increased permeate space-time yield.
items.why_it_matters: The specific fixes that beat fouling at 500 L are directly actionable, and the framing matters as much: at manufacturing scale the limiting variable was the retention device, not the cell line or the feed.

items.title: A kinetically constrained dynamic flux balance analysis model predicts diverse CHO-cell culture process modes and conditions.
items.summary: A kinetically constrained dynamic flux balance analysis model was built on a compact stoichiometric network covering 19 canonical amino acids with phenotype-driven kinetic expressions, taking bioreactor pH, basal and feed media composition, feeding times and inoculation density as inputs and predicting growth rate, titer and nutrient and metabolite profiles. Kinetic parameters were regressed on diverse fed-batch data from CHO VRC01, after which the model gave experimentally validated predictions for intensified fed-batch culture - fed-batch-equivalent titers in shorter duration from high initial cell density and increased feed addition - as well as for perfusion operation and for different media.
items.why_it_matters: A model trained only on fed-batch data that then predicted perfusion and intensified fed-batch is the strongest case yet for using your existing fed-batch dataset to scope a mode change before committing a campaign, with the caveat that it was shown on one cell line.

items.title: Upstream process optimization and its critical role in chimpanzee adenoviral vector clinical drug development: lessons learned from VRON-0200 manufacturing.
items.summary: During development of VRON-0200, a chimpanzee adenoviral (AdC) vector immunotherapy for chronic hepatitis B, the authors found that upstream process optimization rather than downstream purification drove crude harvest quality and final drug product attributes. Iterative refinement of permissive cell growth cycles, time of harvest and multiplicity of infection, guided by a tiered analytical strategy, delivered high-purity harvests with better infectivity ratios, lower host cell residuals and fewer product-related impurities, reducing downstream processing demand; the resulting process supported GMP production and a Phase 1b readout showing safety, tolerability and significant anti-HBV activity.
items.why_it_matters: An explicit upstream-first argument against polishing your way out of a dirty harvest, with the levers named (growth cycles, harvest timing, MOI) and a clinical-stage case attached - exactly the argument DSP counterparts tend to resist.

items.title: Integrated Continuous Biomanufacturing of Recombinant Adeno-Associated Virus.
items.venue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
items.summary: A bioRxiv preprint describes an integrated continuous rAAV platform that couples perfusion culture to semi-continuous twin-column affinity capture (CaptureSMB), capturing only extracellular rAAV and so eliminating chemical cell lysis, depth filtration and endonuclease treatment, with stable operation sustained over five days. Against conventional batch processing, perfusion improved capsid or vector genome yield depending on the production process, and affinity capture alone brought total DNA down to batch-comparable levels with no measurable loss of impurity clearance or potency.
items.why_it_matters: The notable claim is the unit operations deleted rather than the yield - this is the architecture to borrow when costing a continuous vector process, bearing in mind it is a preprint and the yield benefit was process-dependent.

items.title: Developing affordable monoclonal antibodies for LMICs through high performance manufacturing processes and LMIC based commercial manufacturing.
items.summary: High-productivity, high-yield fed-batch production was demonstrated with clonal variants of ZAC-3, a mAb against the conserved core and lipid A region of Vibrio cholerae lipopolysaccharide, and those run data were then extrapolated to a continuous manufacturing approach to argue a viable path to low-cost commercial supply, further reduced by manufacturing in an LMIC-based GMP facility.
items.why_it_matters: The continuous manufacturing economics are extrapolated from fed-batch data rather than demonstrated, so read this as a COGS argument for low-dose infectious-disease mAbs rather than as process evidence.

items.title: Evaluation of media intensification strategies in perfusion.
items.summary: Two media intensification strategies aimed at cutting perfusion rate by up to 30 percent were compared: a concentrated basal formulation and a commercial perfusion-rate-reducing supplement. Direct concentration stalled cell growth by raising osmolality and ultimately lowered viability, while the supplement maintained viability and productivity with no significant product quality impact, and the result generalized to a different medium and clone. Cell cycle analysis showed both strategies arrest cells in G0/G1, but the supplement arrested proliferation more effectively, suggesting a larger shift from growth-driven glycolytic cells to production-driven oxidative metabolism.
items.why_it_matters: Concentrating the perfusion medium is the obvious way to cut volumetric media spend and this says it fails on osmolality; the G0/G1 and oxidative-shift reading also tells you to measure cell cycle distribution, not just VCD and titer, when evaluating any perfusion rate reduction.

items.title: Integrated extractive fermentation of laccase using aqueous biphasic systems: From production to functional coatings.
items.summary: Extractive fermentation of Trametes versicolor laccase expressed in Komagataella phaffii was integrated with aqueous biphasic systems so that production, recovery and primary purification happen in one step. A polymer-polymer system of 10.0 wt percent PEG 8000 with 5.0 wt percent dextran 40000 performed best, giving a 19 percent increase in laccase activity recovered in the dextran-rich phase, 4.6-fold purification and 464.7 U/L recovery against a buffer control, and the recovered enzyme retained catalytic efficiency and was used to synthesize polydopamine coatings on PMMA.
items.why_it_matters: Integrating recovery into the fermenter is the intensification idea worth noting, but an aqueous two-phase system in a yeast enzyme process has no path into a CHO mAb train.

categories.name: Process Modeling, Digital Twins & Statistical Learning
categories.synthesis: Where September's spine here was benchmarking and the field's own complaint about missing shared datasets, this month supplies both some datasets and the sharpest available caution about what a well-performing model proves. The fault-inclusive soft sensing preprint is the item to read: on simulated penicillin batches, including deviation batches in training cut pooled RMSE on held-out deviations from 3.195 to 2.564 g/L and lifted R2 from 0.858 to 0.909 with normal-operation error unchanged, yet one deviation batch stayed at R2 -2.48, and a fault-risk classifier, an Isolation Forest out-of-distribution detector and empirical error ranges all returned incomplete reliability information - so a soft sensor validated on normal operation says nothing about the deviations you would most want it for. On the dataset gap, the NISTCHO reference process and the EXPERT metadata template are two answers of different kinds, and the industrial fed-batch benchmarking study is a third, working from a published dataset and showing that the imputation choice sits upstream of everything else, with LightGBM selected specifically because it preserved observed measurements exactly. The models built on real process data are the ones to take seriously: the kinetically constrained dFBA trained on fed-batch CHO data and validated on perfusion and intensified fed-batch, and the age-structured adenovirus model that identified glucose per cell at infection as the best proxy for the cell density effect and predicted titers to roughly 2 to 2.6 times assay standard deviation. The scale-up study adds a design rule with a sting, that the optimal greyness of a hybrid model under data scarcity is not the one you would pick with abundant data, so a structure validated on a rich process should not be ported to a thin one; BioOps supplies the lifecycle governance half, and the four reviews plus the clinical observation-scheduling and microalgae reinforcement-learning preprints are off-platform.

items.summary: A kinetically constrained dynamic flux balance analysis model was built on a compact stoichiometric network covering 19 canonical amino acids with phenotype-driven kinetic expressions, taking bioreactor pH, basal and feed media composition, feeding times and inoculation density as inputs and predicting growth rate, titer and nutrient and metabolite profiles. Kinetic parameters were regressed on diverse fed-batch data from CHO VRC01, after which the model gave experimentally validated predictions for intensified fed-batch culture - fed-batch-equivalent titers in shorter duration from high initial cell density and increased feed addition - as well as for perfusion operation and for different media.

items.title: Sequence optimization targeting mRNA stability enhances monoclonal antibody titers in CHO cells.
items.summary: A combinatorial library of synonymous IgG1 light-chain coding variants was integrated as single copies at one defined CHO genomic locus with identical regulatory elements, and steady-state mRNA abundance measured by deep sequencing of gDNA and mRNA served as a proxy for mRNA stability. Those data trained a model predicting abundance from coding sequence using nucleotide-transformer embeddings, which was combined with established translational metrics in a genetic algorithm for multi-objective codon optimization. Trastuzumab sequences optimized for high rather than low abundance raised intracellular mRNA 41 percent, titer 59 percent and cell-specific productivity 85 percent with comparable viable cell densities, and against sequences from two commercial providers achieved 70 percent higher titer and 98 percent higher cell-specific productivity.
items.why_it_matters: The single-copy defined-locus design removes the copy-number confounder, making this a credible claim that a vendor codon-optimized sequence leaves most of the available expression unclaimed - and the lever costs nothing at the DNA design stage.

items.title: Data-Driven Approach for Bioreactor Monitoring and Prediction in Monoclonal Antibody Production.
items.summary: A previously published industrial fed-batch mAb dataset was rebuilt end to end: eight supervised regressors were compared for imputation, with LightGBM selected because it preserved all observed measurements exactly and reproduced both marginal distributions and multivariate geometry better than a published dual-hybrid method. Thirty-four single and stacked models were then benchmarked for pointwise titer soft sensing (test R2 up to 0.98) and early prediction of final titer from days 1-7 (0.93), with nonlinear tree ensembles beating linear and kernel models and stacking adding modest consistent gains. Permutation importance, SHAP and partial dependence put elapsed culture time, total cell density, culture volume, glutamine and glutamate at the top, while glucose and pH contributed little within the operating range.
items.why_it_matters: The variable importance result is the usable part: the loops you hold tightly at setpoint carry almost no predictive information, so feed a titer soft sensor culture age, cell mass, volume and the glutamine/glutamate pair instead.

items.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Generic Raman Model for Commercial-Scale Cell Culture Process Monitoring.
items.summary: In-line Raman spectra from four distinct 1500-L commercial CHO fed-batch processes were aggregated into one generic model; 15 combinations of regression algorithm and feature selection were screened, then representative pipelines were tested under repeated batch-level validation splits. A support vector machine with interval whale optimization feature selection held R2 above 0.94 for glucose, lactate and viable cell density on an independent test set, with SHAP and permutation importance pointing at chemically plausible vibrational regions. Transfer to a fifth unseen commercial process exposed the limits of the global model and required local updating with a limited set of labeled spectra.
items.why_it_matters: First commercial-scale evidence that one Raman calibration can span multiple products, with the honest limit attached - budget a small labeled set per new process rather than assuming a global model removes recalibration.

items.title: Mechanistic Digital Model for Real-Time Monitoring and Optimization of Adenovirus Production.
items.summary: Working on adenovirus production, the authors screened indicators of the cell density effect and identified glucose availability per cell at time of infection as the most effective proxy, then built an age-structured mechanistic model linking glucose and viable cell density to viral production while reproducing the density/productivity trade-off. The model predicted viral particle titers in batch and fed-batch at RMSE 0.39 log10 IVP/mL for infectious particles and 0.20 log10 VP/mL for total particles, about 2.6 and 2.0 times the respective assay standard deviations.
items.why_it_matters: For infection-based processes, glucose per cell at infection is a cheaper handle on the cell density effect than the usual density and MOI grid; for a CHO mAb process the transferable lesson is the proxy selection, not the model.

items.title: Towards Digital-Twin-Enabled Bioprocess Monitoring: Fault-Inclusive Soft Sensing of Penicillin Concentration Under Process Deviations
items.summary: A bioRxiv preprint tested whether a soft sensor that performs well in normal operation can be trusted during deviations, using 100 simulated IndPenSim penicillin batches (90 normal, 10 documented deviations, 113,935 observations) and a matched comparison of normal-only against fault-inclusive HistGradientBoosting regressors on 36 current and causal history inputs. On held-out deviation batches, fault-inclusive training cut pooled RMSE from 3.195 to 2.564 g/L and MAE from 2.076 to 1.441 g/L and raised R2 from 0.8580 to 0.9085 with normal-operation RMSE essentially unchanged (1.981 against 1.983), improving eight of ten deviation batches; batch 100 still failed badly at RMSE 6.631 and R2 -2.4837, and a fault-risk classifier, an Isolation Forest out-of-distribution detector and empirical error ranges all gave incomplete reliability information.
items.why_it_matters: The honest conclusion is the useful one: validating a soft sensor on normal operation tells you nothing about its behavior during the deviations you would most want it for, and neither OOD detection nor empirical error bands closed that gap here.

items.title: Enabling Bioprocess Upscaling Prediction Through Hybrid Modelling and Transfer Learning Under Small-Data Scenarios.
items.summary: Hybrid modeling was combined with transfer learning to predict industrial-scale dynamics from a high-fidelity model built on limited lab-scale data and adapted using pilot-scale information only. On a real yeast fermentation case the framework reached 23.2 percent mean absolute percentage error at industrial scale. The study also found that the greyness of the hybrid model - how much mechanism versus how much learned function - decisively governs both predictive accuracy and whether transfer learning is feasible at all, and that the optimal level under data scarcity differs from the data-rich case.
items.why_it_matters: The greyness finding is the usable one: do not port a hybrid structure validated on a data-rich process into a thin one, because the right mechanistic/empirical balance changes with how much data you have.

items.title: BioOps: Enabling MLOps for scalable and flexible model-centric process control in biopharmaceutical development.
items.summary: BioOps is a modular automation framework for advanced process control that imports MLOps practice into the control stack: version-controlled model registries, containerized deployment and CI/CD pipelines, with model development explicitly decoupled from model execution so models and control strategies can be deployed and refined without vendor-specific integration. Case studies across a geographically distributed set of bioreactors cover PAT-driven feedback control, hybrid model-based nutrient and glucose feeding, adaptive phase transitions and cross-scale deployment, with traceability and model lifecycle management embedded.
items.why_it_matters: This is the model-governance half of a control strategy, which is exactly what a reviewer will ask for once a soft sensor becomes a control input - note that no control performance numbers are reported, only architecture and deployments.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in bioanalytics: implications for research and education.
items.summary: A discussion piece on AI in bioanalytics arguing that predictive performance only counts where model outputs can be tied to biologically, chemically or physically meaningful processes, and treating black-box, grey-box and white-box models as complementary rather than competing. Grey-box and hybrid strategies are identified as best suited to bioanalytical work because they combine data-driven learning with domain knowledge, illustrated by a UV/Vis spectroscopic case study on mammalian cell viability that pairs physics-informed AI with experimental design and model validation; the remainder addresses curriculum implications.
items.why_it_matters: A position piece whose only concrete content is the UV/Vis viability case study; the grey-box argument is already better made with benchmarks in the bioprocess hybrid-modeling literature.

items.title: From Learning to Control: Data-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multivariable Control in a Microalgae Bioprocess
items.summary: An arXiv preprint proposing a hybrid offline-online multi-agent reinforcement learning scheme for simultaneous pH and dissolved oxygen control in microalgae photobioreactors, using DDPG agents trained entirely on historical data generated by an expert system so no exploratory experimentation on the plant is needed. After deployment the agents run autonomously and retune their policies daily to track evolving dynamics and reject fast disturbances, and the framework was validated in an open industrial-scale photobioreactor under realistic conditions.
items.why_it_matters: Offline training on historical expert-system data with online adaptation is a plausible answer to the objection that reinforcement learning has to break reactors to learn, but the demonstration is open microalgae culture and no control performance metrics are given.

items.title: How AI Can Advance Mathematical Biology: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions.
items.summary: A review organizing the uses of AI and machine learning in mathematical biology, holding that mechanistic models remain central for structure, interpretability and insight while AI serves prediction, hybrid modeling, inference and control where data are high-dimensional, noisy, heterogeneous or incomplete. Examples span biomedical, epidemiological, ecological, evolutionary, biochemical and population-level systems, with interpretability, identifiability, generalization and uncertainty quantification named as the recurring threats to biological credibility.
items.why_it_matters: Not a bioprocess paper; the identifiability and uncertainty-quantification framing carries over, but it carries over better from the bioprocess hybrid-modeling work in the same category.

items.title: INFORME: coupling information-theoretic experimental design with nonlinear mixed-effects modeling for efficient observation scheduling
items.summary: A bioRxiv preprint presenting INFORME, which couples Bayesian information-theoretic experimental design with nonlinear mixed-effects modeling to choose each patient's next measurement time adaptively, ranking candidate times by expected reduction in patient-specific parameter uncertainty under population and subgroup priors. On 150 synthetic prostate spheroid trajectories the protocol dropped from nine scans to three or four with both pretreatment scans omitted, and on 39 head-and-neck patients from six scans to three with better prediction from delaying the first on-treatment scan; across both datasets adaptive schedules used a mean of 2.7 scans instead of seven and advanced patient-specific prediction by a mean of 15.5 days (95 percent CI 6.7-24.3).
items.why_it_matters: Clinical scheduling rather than bioprocess, but the mechanism - population priors plus expected uncertainty reduction to pick the next sampling time - is exactly what you would want for deciding when to pull offline reference samples in a sparse-sampling campaign.

items.title: "EXPERT" A Practical and Forward-Looking Guide to Capturing Protein Expression and Purification Metadata to develop Machine Learning Models.
items.summary: EXPERT is a structured reporting template for protein expression and purification metadata, assembled from academic and industry input and distilled to the parameter set judged sufficient both for workflow reproducibility and for building machine learning models on pooled data.
items.why_it_matters: Nothing to run, but if you are assembling a historical dataset for modeling, adopting an existing metadata schema is cheaper than inventing one and keeps your data poolable later.

items.title: Industry-defined opportunities for advancing big data capabilities in biopharmaceutical manufacturing
items.summary: No abstract was indexed for this item and no venue was recorded, so nothing can be said about its content beyond the title: an industry-defined set of opportunities for advancing big data capabilities in biopharmaceutical manufacturing. What those opportunities are, who defined them and on what evidence are all unknown from what is available here.
items.why_it_matters: Unverifiable as indexed - retrieve the full text before citing it for anything.

items.title: A Review on Applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Monoclonal Antibody (mAb) Manufacturing.
items.summary: A review surveying artificial intelligence applications across mAb manufacturing - upstream and downstream processing, process control, optimization, product property monitoring and regulatory compliance - with case studies on predictive modeling for cell culture optimization, media formulation and bioreactor control, plus process monitoring, fault detection and real-time decision-making.
items.why_it_matters: A broad survey with no new data; useful only as a citation for an internal AI strategy document.

categories.name: Cell Line Development & Clone Selection
categories.synthesis: This month's gains come from the cassette rather than the clone, and one paper explains why clone ranking is noisy in the first place. Treating mRNA stability as a design parameter - steady-state abundance measured across a synonymous light-chain library integrated as single copies at one defined locus, then predicted from sequence and optimized by genetic algorithm - gave 41 percent more mRNA, 59 percent more titer and 85 percent higher cell-specific productivity against low-abundance designs and, more usefully, 70 percent higher titer and 98 percent higher qP against two commercial codon-optimization providers, which extends August's synonymous-codon result with a new and quantified axis. The synthetic promoter work makes the same move inside a site-specific integration platform, with landing-pad-specific promoters matching or exceeding CMV at a third of its length and lifting monospecific fed-batch titer up to 45 percent, and it carries its own correction: for a bispecific, the pure synthetic combination gave about 2.7 g/L against about 3.8 g/L for all-CMV, so the gain is format- and cassette-dependent rather than a promoter you can adopt wholesale. Against both, SEC-seq found endpoint IgG transcript abundance and accumulated secretion only moderately coupled in single cells, with three high-secreting clones converging on a translation-focused state but arriving through different energy and redox programs - glycolytic with UPR activation, oxidative phosphorylation with fatty acid beta-oxidation, or modest central carbon - which means no single metabolic marker will rank clones, and extends September's point that titer-only selection hides what a line is spending its resource on. The barcoded Sleeping Beauty work is the stability caution worth keeping: secondary transposition is not random, depending on linear distance and on Hi-C contacts with the donor locus within about 50 kb, which matters if your platform leaves transposase expressed longer than it needs to be. The rest - a quad-guide knockout protocol, a rabbit single-B-cell discovery workflow, an rDNA-targeting retrotransposon shown for gene therapy, a bovine oviduct line and a CHO-produced anti-PD-1 nonclinical package - carry no CHO production content.

items.title: SEC-seq reveals translation-focused metabolic strategies for high IgG productivity in clonal CHO cells.
items.summary: Secretion EnCoded single-cell sequencing (SEC-seq) measured transcriptomes and secreted IgG simultaneously in single cells from a parental production line and five CHO clones of differing cell-specific productivity. Endpoint IgG mRNA abundance and accumulated IgG secretion were only moderately coupled across single cells, so transcript abundance sampled once does not explain intra-clonal secretion heterogeneity. Cells accommodating the recombinant expression burden had more active translation-associated pathways and suppressed energy-intensive processing of endogenous secreted proteins; three high-secreting clones converged on that translation-focused state but differed in subpopulation composition and in the energy and redox programs coupled to IgG output - one low-growth, glycolytic, NAD and one-carbon associated with UPR activation, one with raised oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid beta-oxidation, and one with more modest central-carbon and mitochondrial lipid metabolism - with Aldoa, Ndufab1, Acsl5 and Mthfd2 showing clone-specific correlation with IgG.
items.why_it_matters: It explains why ranking clones on transcript level or bulk titer is noisy, and because the energy and redox route to a high-secreting state differs clone to clone, no single metabolic screening marker will generalize across your panel.

items.title: Sequence optimization targeting mRNA stability enhances monoclonal antibody titers in CHO cells.
items.summary: A combinatorial library of synonymous IgG1 light-chain coding variants was integrated as single copies at one defined CHO genomic locus with identical regulatory elements, and steady-state mRNA abundance measured by deep sequencing of gDNA and mRNA served as a proxy for mRNA stability. Those data trained a model predicting abundance from coding sequence using nucleotide-transformer embeddings, which was combined with established translational metrics in a genetic algorithm for multi-objective codon optimization. Trastuzumab sequences optimized for high rather than low abundance raised intracellular mRNA 41 percent, titer 59 percent and cell-specific productivity 85 percent with comparable viable cell densities, and against sequences from two commercial providers achieved 70 percent higher titer and 98 percent higher cell-specific productivity.
